title: The index is ODD at the prize, so the constant-index lane can never recurse via a 2-power head: F8 and F20 live on coprime-order sides of F_q*≅μ_n×ℤ/m
evidence: C085 rests on two algebraic facts, both already axiom-clean in-tree AND independently reproduced here exactly. PROVEN HALF (the structural separation): (a) prizeIndex_odd (ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ProximityGap/Frontier/_GaussPhaseFlatnessAlgebra.lean): if n=2^a is the FULL 2-part of q-1 (padicValNat 2 (q-1)=a) then m=(q-1)/n is odd. (b) doubling_bijective_of_odd (same file): x->x+x is bijective on any finite additive group of odd order; instantiated at ℤ/m it makes the Hasse-Davenport order-2 'doubling' a PERMUTATION of the m-phase index, not a 2-to-1 fold. Fast-iterate elaboration of that file is green (32s), axiom audit shows only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx (verified via scripts/pg-iterate.sh). My probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C085_index_parity.py (exact integer arithmetic, sympy isprime) confirms in the STRICT prize regime — n=2^mu a PROPER subgroup (n^2<q), q prime ~n^beta (beta in {4,5}), n=the full 2-part — across 16 instances (mu=3,4,5,6 × beta=4,5 × 2 primes each, q up to 1.07e9): m=(q-1)/n is ODD in 16/16 and x->2x is a BIJECTION of ℤ/m in 16/16 (image size = m every time). ROBUSTNESS: when n=2^mu is DEFICIENT (not the full 2-part, 2^{mu+1}|q-1), m is EVEN and doubling collapses 2-to-1 (image=m/2) — so the parity fact is exactly equivalent to the prize 'full 2-part' convention. The completion sum that carries the house lives over t=m phases indexed by ℤ/m (matches SubgroupGaussSumWorstCase.completion_identity with d=n, t=(q-1)/n), so the F8 dyadic descent (M(n)^2<=2M(n/2)^2), which needs a 2-to-1 order-2 fold, has no order-2 lever there: F8 acts on μ_n=2^a, the DFT flatness question lives on the coprime odd-order ℤ/m of the splitting F_q^* ≅ μ_n × ℤ/m. This no-go is CORRECT.
reduced_to: After removing the (dead) 2-power-fold lever on the index, the prize residual is exactly flatness of the m-DFT of the unimodular Gauss-phase sequence (a_j = τ(ψ^j)/√q) over the ODD-order cyclic group ℤ/m — i.e. effective Jacobi-sum/Salem–Zygmund equidistribution at constant index (F16), with NO dyadic tower. This is the same open √-cancellation core, restated on the odd side.
wall: W-BGK (and W-LamLeung): the unproven half is the m-phase flatness over odd-order ℤ/m, which is the BGK/Paley √-cancellation problem for thin μ_n; Lam–Leung governs only char-0 antipodal vanishing on the 2-power side μ_n, which the dyadic-tower verdict already showed is upward pressure, not a cancellation lever.
honest_note: PARTIAL, not a closure. The PROVEN half (parity + doubling bijection => no 2-power fold on the index) is genuine, axiom-clean in-tree, and I reproduced it exactly in the strict prize regime (16/16, plus the deficient-case robustness flip). But this is a NO-GO for one specific lever (the 2-adic/parallelogram fold F8 cannot be combined with the index DFT F20), not a flatness bound — the file itself disclaims any δ* pin. It is essentially the INDEX-SIDE reformulation of Wall 1 of the already-logged dyadic-2adic-gauss-tower verdict (docs/kb/deltastar-407-dyadic-2adic-gauss-tower-verdict-2026-06-13.md): the √-cancellation phases are all odd-order characters in ℤ/m, untouchable by any 2-adic lever; the descent-content half was separately found content-free in verdict_C072 (the parallelogram inflates, never controls). So C085 sharpens WHERE the wall sits (the odd-order index group) and correctly forecloses the F8∘F20 combination, but does not advance past restating the BGK/Paley core. No in-tree theorem is refuted (the cited Lean lemmas are correct; C085 over-reads them only insofar as it is presented as 'insight' rather than 'no-go'). Probe is exact integer arithmetic, strict prize regime, no full-group/small-prime false positives.
